newsitem.title: INDIA: India's RBI relaxes rules for bank remittances.
newsitem.headline: India's RBI relaxes rules for bank remittances.

text.p: The Reserve Bank of India said on Thursday it had removed ceilings on foreign exchange remittances by banks for the following purposes:
* Maintenance expenses of representatives posted abroad by Indian newspapers/news agencies and periodicals
* Charges incurred towards electronics database costs including charges for computer connections/time, software, etc.
* Annual maintenance/service charges for imported machinery, software, etc.
* Actual cost of advertisements in print media abroad
* Initial expenses for opening of overseas non-trading offices/representative offices by eligible exporters
* Actual cost of imports of designs and drawings
* Actual cost of goods imported through post parcel
* Expenses incurred towards legal services relating to import transactions
* Amount of retainer's fees payable to the overseas agents
* Remittances towards solicitors' fees/average adjusters' fees by Indian shipping companies.
"The removal of these limits which covers a wide area will reduce delay and thus further facilitate all current account transactions," Reserve Bank said in a statement.
